note: Ship canals and narrow straits the routing charts cannot represent as connected water (they are narrower than a chart cell). Each is a gameplay abstraction: a navigable link along approximate real centreline points through real water, from an open-water entrance on one side to one on the other. The points are approximate (place names given); locks, rules, tolls and traffic are not modelled. The Panama Canal is carved into the world chart instead (see data/navigation/world/world.json, 'canal'). Not for navigation.

canals.name: Kiel Canal
canals.description: The Kiel Canal (Nord-Ostsee-Kanal) from Kiel-Holtenau on the Baltic to Brunsbuettel on the Elbe and the North Sea.
points: Kiel Fjord, off the Holtenau locks

canals.name: Suez Canal
canals.description: The Suez Canal from Port Said on the Mediterranean to Port Tewfik (Suez), continued down the Gulf of Suez past the Strait of Gubal into the open Red Sea: on the world chart the Gulf of Suez is a strip of water not connected at Gubal.
points: the Gulf of Suez, off Suez
the Gulf of Suez, off Ras Gharib
the Red Sea, beyond the Strait of Gubal

canals.name: Bab-el-Mandeb
canals.description: The strait between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, through its western channel past Perim island. On the world chart it is narrower than a cell, so the Red Sea would otherwise be closed.
points: the Red Sea, north of the strait
